```{r setup, include=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr) 
library(readr)







# Import data
genes_data   <- read_csv("D:/2025_summer/R/QBS103_GSE157103_genes.csv",
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
series_matrix <- read_csv("D:/2025_summer/R/QBS103_GSE157103_series_matrix-1.csv",
                          show_col_types = FALSE)

# Pivot gene expression to long format
expr_long <- genes_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -1,
    names_to  = "participant_id",
    values_to = "expression"
  ) %>%
  rename(gene = 1)

# Clean metadata: rename CRP column, parse it, trim factors
meta_df <- series_matrix %>%
  rename(crp = `crp(mg/l)`) %>%
  mutate(
    crp        = parse_number(crp),
    sex        = factor(str_trim(sex)),
    icu_status = factor(str_trim(icu_status), levels = c("no", "yes"))
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, crp, sex, icu_status)

#  Define the plotting function
plot_gene_plots <- function(data, gene_list,
                            cont_var, cat_var1, cat_var2) {
  # Filter to genes and drop missing covariates
  df <- data %>%
    filter(gene %in% gene_list) %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c(cont_var, cat_var1, cat_var2)))
  
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    stop("No data to plot: check your gene names or covariates.")
  }
  
  for (g in gene_list) {
    sub <- df %>% filter(gene == g)
    
    # 1. Histogram of expression
    p_hist <- ggplot(sub, aes(x = expression)) +
      geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1,
                     fill    = "#2c7fb8",
                     color   = "white") +
      labs(title = paste("Histogram of", g, "Expression"),
           x     = paste(g, "Expression"),
           y     = "Count") +
      theme_minimal()
    print(p_hist)
    
    # 2. Scatterplot vs continuous covariate
    p_scatter <- ggplot(sub,
                        aes_string(x     = cont_var,
                                   y     = "expression",
                                   color = cat_var1,
                                   shape = cat_var2)) +
      geom_point(size  = 2.5,
                 alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm",
                  se     = FALSE,
                  linetype = "dashed",
                  color   = "gray30") +
      labs(title = paste(g, "Expression vs", cont_var),
           x     = cont_var,
           y     = paste(g, "Expression"),
           color = cat_var1,
           shape = cat_var2) +
      theme_minimal()
    print(p_scatter)
    
    # 3. Boxplot by two categorical covariates
    p_box <- ggplot(sub,
                    aes_string(x    = cat_var1,
                               y    = "expression",
                               fill = cat_var2)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1) +
      scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2",
                        name    = cat_var2) +
      labs(title = paste(g, "Expression by", cat_var1, "&", cat_var2),
           x     = cat_var1,
           y     = paste(g, "Expression")) +
      theme_minimal()
    print(p_box)
  }
}

#  Merge expr_long + meta_df
merged_df <- expr_long %>%
  left_join(meta_df, by = "participant_id")

# Call the function for your genes
plot_gene_plots(
  data      = merged_df,
  gene_list = c("ABCA1"), # gene name
  cont_var  = "crp", # continuous covariate
  cat_var1  = "sex", # categorical
  cat_var2  = "icu_status" # categorical
)




```
```{r}
genes_list <- c("ABCA1", "A2M", "A1BG") # list of genes
for (gene in genes_list) {
  plot_gene_plots(
    data      = merged_df,
    gene_list = gene,
    cont_var  = "crp",
    cat_var1  = "sex",
    cat_var2  = "icu_status"
  )
}
```
